title: Laila + Ayelet:
headline: A Palestinian mother and an Israeli co-CEO, both bereaved, sit side by side and ask us to be pro-peace.
story: Laila is a Palestinian mother whose son died in 2002. Ayelet is the Israeli co-CEO of the Parents Circle – Families Forum. She lost her eldest brother in 1982. Both chose not to take revenge. They share the same pain and the same tears.

Their lesson: give yourself one minute to listen to the other side and see their humanity. Their ask: not pro-Israel, not pro-Palestine, but pro-peace. The two of them together is the point. Respectful, never dramatic, and hopeful at the end.
do: Open on frame 1 on “but pro-peace” with both women on screen.
Keep their English exactly as spoken (“my son was passed away” stays).
Both women on screen at 00:00, on “we share the same pain”, and at the end.
One name super per woman, on her first solo line.
Tell the son’s story in her words, short and plain.
dont: Do not use 09:33–09:47 or 10:09–10:29. This cut stays on the two of them, not on politics.
No music swell, slow motion or sound effects on the son’s death.
No text that takes a side. No interviewer or retake chatter.
No camera-shutter sounds. No choppy jump cuts.

decisions.t: How to keep both women in a 9:16 frame
decisions.b: The brief asks for both women in frame. A 9:16 crop of the two-shot cannot do it. This plan uses a stacked split screen (Laila top, Ayelet bottom). Yes, or a letterboxed 16:9 two-shot inside the vertical frame?
The chosen bites run about 2:10, not the 80–95 s in the brief. Keep all, or drop 02:47–02:58 and 04:59–05:12 to land near 1:50?
The folder only gives first names. Annelies Van Erp’s subject list is still owed.
